summary: Adds an admin route that deletes one user by id and a purge route that deletes a list of user ids.

findings.title: Delete user route lacks admin check
findings.problem: The DELETE /users/:id route has no requireAdmin middleware. Its sibling routes in the same router both use requireAdmin.
findings.consequence: Any caller who reaches the server can delete any user by id. Attackers can enumerate ids to wipe accounts.
findings.fix: Add requireAdmin to the route before the handler.

findings.title: Purge drops removal promises and reports success early
findings.problem: The purge handler passes an async callback to forEach, so nobody awaits or catches the removeUser promises. db.removeUser throws for an unknown id, which causes an unhandled rejection.
findings.consequence: One unknown id can crash the Node process through the unhandled rejection. The handler also reports every id as removed before any deletion finishes or fails.
findings.fix: Await Promise.allSettled over ids.map(removeUser). Then report the count of fulfilled results.
findings.suggested_change:
const results = await Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: results.filter((r) => r.status === "fulfilled").length });

findings.title: New delete and purge routes have no tests
findings.problem: This change adds two routes with new auth and error paths. No test file in the repository exercises these routes.
findings.consequence: Regressions in authorization or the purge error handling can ship unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests for the auth rejection, the unknown id case and the purge count.
